title: Estimating When You Really Don't Know
meta: B2 · 约 270 词 · 场景：排期估时

sections.heading: 1. Why Single Numbers Mislead
paragraphs: Your PM asks how long the new search integration will take.
You have never used this vendor's API, and the data format is still undecided.
Any single number you give right now is a guess dressed up as a plan.
The usual mistake is to say "about three weeks" to sound ==decisive==.
The PM writes it on the roadmap, and from that moment the guess __becomes a commitment__.
When it slips, the team looks ==unreliable==, even though the original number was never real.
**An estimate without a range is a promise you didn't mean to make.**
Ranges can sound ==noncommittal==, but they carry real information: how much you still don't know.
A wide range is not a weakness; it is an honest description of the problem.
sections.heading_zh: 1. 单个数字为什么会误导
paragraphs_zh: PM 问你新的搜索集成要多久。
你从来没用过这家供应商的 API，数据格式也还没定。
现在你给出的任何一个数字，都只是一个打扮成计划的猜测。
常见的错误是为了显得果断，张口就说「大概三周」。
PM 把它写进 roadmap，从那一刻起，这个猜测就变成了承诺。
等延期了，团队就显得不靠谱，尽管最初那个数字本来就不是真的。
不带区间的估时，是一个你本没打算做出的承诺。
区间听起来可能像不愿表态，但它承载着真实的信息：你还有多少不知道。
区间宽不是弱点；它是对问题的诚实描述。

sections.heading: 2. A Range, a Reason, a Checkpoint
paragraphs: Give a range, and say what drives the width.
"Two to six weeks; the big unknown is whether their API supports bulk updates."
Now the PM knows which question matters most, and might even help answer it.
Spend two or three days on a quick ==prototype== against the real API.
After that, you can give a much tighter estimate, and the PM can decide whether the project is still worth it.
Agree on a ==checkpoint== where you will update the number, and put it in the calendar.
**The goal is not a perfect estimate; it is an estimate that gets better on schedule.**
When the update arrives on the day you promised, a changed number looks like ==diligence==, not failure.
Over a few projects, that habit __earns you__ more trust than any confident guess ever could.
sections.heading_zh: 2. 一个区间、一个理由、一个检查点
paragraphs_zh: 给一个区间，并说明是什么让它这么宽。
「两到六周；最大的未知是他们的 API 支不支持批量更新。」
这样 PM 就知道哪个问题最关键，说不定还能帮着去搞清楚。
然后主动提出把区间缩小。
花两三天对着真实的 API 快速做一个原型。
之后你就能给出一个准得多的估时，PM 也能判断这个项目还值不值得做。
约好一个更新数字的检查点，并且放进日历。
目标不是一次完美的估时；而是一个能按时变得越来越准的估时。
当更新在你承诺的那天准时到来，数字变了看起来是认真负责，而不是失败。
做过几个项目之后，这个习惯为你赢得的信任，比任何自信满满的猜测都多。

gist.q: 面对未知时给出单一数字有什么问题？
gist.a: 猜测会被写进路线图变成承诺，延期时团队显得不可靠，尽管原始数字本来就不真实。
给一个区间，并说明是什么因素决定了区间宽度（最大的未知是什么）。

gist.q: 如何让估时逐步变准并赢得信任？
gist.a: 花两三天做原型缩小不确定性；约定检查点按时更新数字，这样数字变化看起来是尽责而非失败。

prompts.q: PM 在会上追问“接入新支付渠道要多久？给个数”。你们从没接过这家。用 30 秒给出区间、主要未知和检查点。
prompts.ref: Honestly, a single number right now would be a guess. My range is three to eight weeks. The biggest unknown is their refund API; if it works like their docs say, we're near the low end. Here's what I suggest: give us three days to build a small prototype against their sandbox. On Thursday I'll come back with a much tighter estimate, and you can decide if it's still worth it.
prompts.ref_zh: 说实话，现在给一个数字只能是猜。我的区间是三到八周。最大的未知是他们的退款 API；如果它跟文档说的一样，我们就接近下限。我的建议是：给我们三天，对着他们的沙箱环境做个小原型。周四我给你一个准得多的估时，到时候你再判断还值不值得做。

prompts.q: 上次估三周、实际做了六周，老板有些不满。用 30 秒说明你以后会怎么给估时。
prompts.ref: You're right that the last estimate was off, and I take responsibility for that. The problem was that I gave one number when we still didn't understand the data migration. From now on, I'll give a range and name the biggest unknown behind it. I'll also set a checkpoint after the first week to update the estimate, so you hear about any change early rather than at the deadline.
prompts.ref_zh: 你说得对，上次的估时偏了，这个责任在我。问题在于，我们还没搞懂数据迁移的时候，我就给了一个数字。以后我会给区间，并说明背后最大的未知是什么。我还会在第一周之后设一个检查点来更新估时，这样有任何变化你都能早点知道，而不是到 deadline 才知道。

words.ex: We need someone decisive to own the launch call.
The staging data is unreliable, so test against a production copy.
The vendor was noncommittal about when the fix would be ready.
Let's build a quick prototype before we commit to this design.
We'll have a checkpoint at the end of week two to review progress.
Her diligence in testing caught the bug before launch.
Is this date a commitment or just a target?
We narrowed down the cause to one bad query.
The schedule is tight, so let's not add new scope.
